items.plain: Nachiketas tells Death that riches, pleasures and even a long life are short-lived and drain the senses; Death can keep them, because wealth can never satisfy a person.
items.core_idea: Wealth and pleasure cannot satisfy a human being
items.extended_text: Nachiketas said, “These are merely things of a day, O Death, they wear away the energy of all the sense-organs. Even the longest life is very short. These horses and chariots, dances and songs, may remain with Thee. Man cannot be satisfied by wealth. Can we retain wealth when we behold Thee? We shall live only so long as Thou desires”.

items.plain: Once you see religion and God more vividly than you see the outside world, nothing can shake your belief, just as no one can make you doubt a country you have visited. That is real faith.
items.core_idea: Real faith comes from direct experience of God

items.plain: Joy and sorrow keep vanishing: as a child he thought driving a cab would be perfect happiness, and now he does not. So which joy will you cling to?
items.core_idea: Every joy we chase keeps changing and vanishing

items.plain: What feels like pleasure today may feel like pain tomorrow. The same fire that warms us can burn us, and that is not the fire's fault.
items.core_idea: The same thing can bring pleasure or pain

items.plain: Picture the Self as the rider, the body as the chariot, the intellect as driver, the mind as reins and the senses as horses. Keep senses and mind in control and you reach God; lose control and you are destroyed.
items.core_idea: Control the senses and mind to reach the goal

items.plain: The path is like walking on a razor's edge, long and dangerous, but keep going and do not lose heart. Wake up, get up, and do not stop until you reach the goal.
items.core_idea: Keep striving on the hard path until the goal

items.plain: Desire causes all misery: it keeps you like a beggar, always wanting more. As your power to satisfy desires grows steadily, the desires themselves multiply far faster.
items.core_idea: Desire always outgrows our power to satisfy it

items.plain: Giving up the self is the basis of true life; every good and truly alive moment comes when we are not thinking of ourselves. The small, separate self has to die.
items.core_idea: True life comes from forgetting the separate self

items.plain: In this world, misery follows every happiness like a shadow, and death follows life. They belong together because they are not opposites but two sides of one thing, as are sorrow and joy, good and evil.
items.core_idea: Happiness and misery are two sides of one thing

items.plain: A young man left poor after his father died was told by a clergyman that everything happens for our good. Such comfort is like gold leaf over an old sore: an admission of weakness and absurdity.
items.core_idea: Saying all suffering is good is empty comfort

fix.display_text: I remember when I was young, a young man’s father died and left him poorly off, with a large family to support, and he found that his father’s friends were unwilling to help him. He had a conversation with a clergyman who offered this consolation, “Oh, it is all good, all is sent for our good.” That is the old method of trying to put a piece of gold leaf on an old sore. It is a confession of weakness, of absurdity.

items.plain: Be good and show mercy to those who suffer. But do not try to patch the world up, because nothing will cure it; go beyond it.
items.core_idea: Be kind, but seek to go beyond the world

items.plain: Life is hard and real; push through it bravely, however unyielding it seems. It does not matter, because the soul is stronger.
items.core_idea: The soul is stronger than life's hardships

items.plain: You cause your own suffering and make good and evil; you cover your eyes and complain it is dark. Take your hands away and see the light: you are radiant and already perfect, and always were.
items.core_idea: You are already perfect; stop covering your eyes

items.plain: Moving to a cave, a forest or Varanasi did not bring him clarity, because the same trouble followed him everywhere. We make our own worlds: if I am evil, the whole world looks evil to me.
items.core_idea: We carry our own world wherever we go

items.plain: He wants to know the heart of life itself, what it truly is, not just how it works or what it looks like. He wants the why of everything and leaves the how to children.
items.core_idea: Seek the why of life, not just how

items.plain: A huge river is carrying all of us toward the ocean. Though we sometimes drift aimlessly like bits of straw and paper, in the end we will surely reach the Ocean of Life and Bliss.
items.core_idea: All of us will reach the ocean of bliss

items.plain: One bright idea shines through the superstition of every country and religion: human beings are divine, and divinity is our true nature.
items.core_idea: Human beings are divine by nature

items.plain: Fire lies hidden in flint and dry wood until friction draws it out. In the same way freedom and purity are the very nature of every soul, not qualities, since qualities can be gained and lost.
items.core_idea: Freedom and purity are the soul's very nature

items.plain: Why search for something you never lost, when you are already pure and free? If you think you are free, you are free right now; if you think you are bound, bound you will be.
items.core_idea: You are free if you think you are

items.plain: The moment you say you are bound, weak or helpless, you bring trouble on yourself and add another chain. Do not say it, and do not think it.
items.core_idea: Calling yourself weak binds you further

items.plain: Vedanta says weakness is the one cause of misery: we lie, steal, kill, suffer and even die because we are weak. Where nothing weakens us, there is neither death nor sorrow.
items.core_idea: Weakness is the one cause of suffering

items.plain: However frightening it seems now, one day we will each look back and smile at the superstitions that hid the pure, eternal soul, and say gladly and truly: I am free, always was and always will be.
items.core_idea: One day we will know we were always free

items.plain: Living up to the ideal of being pure is hard, but a child still looks up at the distant sky. Failing to reach truth at once is no reason to drink poison by turning to weakness and superstition.
items.core_idea: A hard ideal is no reason to choose weakness

items.plain: We are at our best when all responsibility is ours, as anyone handed a baby turns selfless. With no devil to blame and no personal God to carry our burdens, I alone make my fate, good or bad.
items.core_idea: Full responsibility brings out our best

items.plain: Water runs down mountains to the ocean, rises as vapour and returns, over and over. All life and everything we know moves this way, like breathing in and out: each wave has its hollow, each hollow its wave.
items.core_idea: All existence moves in cycles of rising and falling

items.plain: A seed does not become a tree at once. It rests and works unseen beneath the soil, breaks apart and seems to decay, and new life grows out of that decay.
items.core_idea: New life grows out of apparent decay

items.plain: O Lord, you are the man and the woman, the strong youth and the old man on crutches; you are in everything, and you are everything.
items.core_idea: God is in and is everything

items.plain: People have always asked whether anything in this fleeting life is lasting: does something survive when the body dies and burns to ash, and if so, where does it come from and where does it go?
items.core_idea: Does anything in us survive death?

items.plain: The soul does not have knowledge, existence or happiness; it is knowledge, existence and happiness itself. Anything that merely has these has borrowed them and reflects them.
items.core_idea: The soul is knowledge, existence and happiness itself

items.plain: None of us came from nothing or will return to nothing. We have always existed and always will, and no power anywhere can undo our existence.
items.core_idea: We have always existed and always will

items.plain: A child learning piano must first watch every key, but after months and years the playing becomes almost automatic. What first took conscious effort later needs no effort of will.
items.core_idea: Practice turns conscious effort into instinct

items.plain: Like eyes that see others but not themselves, we miss our own faults and blame people, God or fate. But we reap what we sow: we make our own fate, and no one else earns blame or praise.
items.core_idea: We make our own fate

items.plain: The wind fills only ships with sails raised; God's mercy blows day and night for saint and sinner alike, so it is not His fault that some are happy and some not. We make our own destiny.
items.core_idea: God's mercy is for all; we make our destiny

items.plain: God's endless mercy is open to everyone, always, and how we use it is up to us. Blame neither people nor God; when you suffer, blame yourself and try to do better.
items.core_idea: When you suffer, blame no one but yourself

items.plain: Admit your suffering is your own doing, so you alone can undo it. Stand up, be brave and strong, take full responsibility for your destiny, and know all the strength you need is within you.
items.core_idea: You made your misery, so you can undo it

items.plain: Let the past go. The whole future lies ahead, and every word, thought and act builds up for you: bad ones lie in wait like tigers, while good ones stand ready like a hundred thousand angels to defend you forever.
items.core_idea: Every thought and deed shapes your future

items.plain: In the rush of life we forget, but when someone we love dies suddenly, the noise stops for a moment and the soul asks the old questions: what comes after this, and what becomes of the soul?
items.core_idea: A loved one's death stirs questions about the soul

items.plain: Nothing moves in a straight line; everything moves in a circle. So no soul can go downhill forever: everything must complete the circle and return to its source.
items.core_idea: Every soul must return to its source

items.plain: A cloud passing the moon makes the moon seem to move, and from a train the land seems to fly. Likewise you are not really coming or going, born or reborn; you are infinite, ever-present, beyond cause and ever free.
items.core_idea: You are not born or reborn; you are infinite

items.plain: Wherever there are two, there is fear, danger and conflict. When everything is One, when everything is God, who is there to hate or fight?
items.core_idea: Where all is One, there is no one to fight

items.plain: You are the One Being in the universe, so what can make you weak or afraid? Stand up and be free; whatever thought or word makes you weak and fearful is the only evil, and must be avoided.
items.core_idea: Whatever makes you weak and afraid is evil

items.plain: Even if suns fall, moons crumble and whole star systems are destroyed, what is that to you? Stand firm like a rock; you cannot be destroyed.
items.core_idea: You are indestructible; nothing can frighten you

items.plain: Foolish people call you sinners and you sit in a corner weeping, but calling you sinners is foolish and wicked. You are all God; how can you see God and call Him a mere man?
items.core_idea: You are not sinners; you are God

items.plain: When you help a poor person, do not feel the slightest pride. Helping is your worship, not something to be proud of.
items.core_idea: Helping the poor is worship, not pride

items.plain: In life we can see that each of us shapes our future every day: today we decide what tomorrow will be, tomorrow we decide the day after, and so on.
items.core_idea: Each day we shape the next

items.plain: The sense of me and mine is the root of all evil in the world. A dualist says his child and property belong not to him but to God, and everything should be held that way.
items.core_idea: Me and mine is the root of evil

items.plain: God draws every soul as a magnet draws a needle. The dualist says a needle caked in clay will not move toward the magnet until the clay is washed off; the soul's evil deeds are that dirt.
items.core_idea: Evil deeds cover the soul's pull toward God

items.plain: We have made ourselves weak, always wanting something to lean on like small plants needing a stake. Many want a comfortable religion; very few ask for truth, fewer dare to learn it, and fewest dare to live it.
items.core_idea: Few dare to seek and live the truth

items.plain: A sick man keeps answering a knock and finding no one, until he realises it was his own heartbeat. So, after seeking God in temples, rivers and heavens, a person finds God is his own Self.
items.core_idea: The God we seek outside is our own Self

items.plain: You are never inside illusion; illusion passes before you. As clouds of every colour come and go across the blue sky and leave it unchanged, you remain forever pure and perfect.
items.core_idea: Like the sky, you stay pure as illusions pass

items.plain: When a person sees himself as one with the Infinite and all separateness melts away, fear, sorrow, jealousy and ill will vanish. Who is left to fear or resent, when there is no one in the universe but I?
items.core_idea: In oneness, fear, sorrow and jealousy vanish

fix.display_text: When man has seen himself as one with the Infinite Being of the universe, when all separateness has ceased, when all men and women, and gods and angels, all animals and plants, and the whole universe have melted into that Oneness, then all fear disappears. Can I hurt myself? Can I kill myself? Can I injure myself? Whom to fear? Can you fear yourself? Then will all sorrow disappear. What can cause me sorrow? I am the One Existence of the universe. Then all jealousies will disappear; of whom to be jealous? Of myself? Then all bad feelings disappear. Against whom can I have bad feeling? Against myself? There is none in the universe but I.

items.plain: Harm no one and dismiss no one's view; meet people where they are and, if you can, help them higher, but never hurt or tear down. Everyone will reach truth in the end.
items.core_idea: Meet people where they are; harm no one

items.plain: Every act and thought leaves an impression on the mind, called samskara in Sanskrit, and all these together form the powerful force we call character. Your character is what you have made of yourself through your actions.
items.core_idea: Character is built from every act and thought

items.plain: Like a caterpillar trapped in the cocoon it spun from its own thread, we have tied ourselves up in our own actions. We set the wheel of cause and effect turning, and now it crushes us.
items.core_idea: We are trapped by our own actions

items.plain: The mind is like a lake and each thought a wave on it. Thought-waves rise and seem to vanish, but they never disappear completely; they become subtler and wait, ready to rise again when called.
items.core_idea: Thoughts never vanish; they wait to rise again

items.plain: To most people nature looks like nothing but a whirling, shifting mass of change. Few ever glimpse the calm sea underneath; to us the universe seems only tossing waves.
items.core_idea: Few glimpse the calm beneath constant change

items.plain: A wave is not truly different from the sea; only its shape and the name we give it set it apart. Take away name and form, and it is the same sea.
items.core_idea: Only name and form separate wave from sea

items.plain: When I read a book, the pages turn, not I; nature is such a book before the soul, scene after scene, while the soul stays the same forever. Birth and death belong to nature, not to you.
items.core_idea: Nature changes; the soul stays the same

items.plain: The worst lie you can tell yourself is that you were born a sinner or wicked. Only the person who sees a sinner in someone else is a sinner.
items.core_idea: Only one who sees sinners is a sinner

items.plain: Crossing a desert, he saw lovely lakes daily until one vanished as he went to drink: a mirage, which he then kept seeing but knew was false. We all travel through the world's mirage without knowing it.
items.core_idea: The world is a mirage we do not recognise

items.plain: Realising truth and merely talking about it are worlds apart; anyone can talk, even parrots. Philosophies, books and churches help in their way, but they fall away once realisation comes, as maps do when you see the country itself.
items.core_idea: Talking about truth is not realising it

items.plain: How can you see evil, a thief or a murderer, unless it is already sitting in your own heart? Be good, and evil will disappear for you.
items.core_idea: Be good and evil disappears for you

items.plain: Bhakti-Yoga is a sincere search for the Lord that begins, goes on and ends in love. A single moment of wildly intense love for God brings eternal freedom.
items.core_idea: One moment of intense love for God frees us

items.plain: In every religion and country, weak and immature minds can love their own ideal only by hating every other one.
items.core_idea: Weak minds love their ideal by hating others

items.plain: A bird needs two wings and a tail to fly. Knowledge is one wing, love of God the other, and yoga is the tail that keeps the balance.
items.core_idea: Knowledge, love and yoga must work together

items.plain: A prayer: as I keep meditating on You, may I never lose the same unfailing love that ignorant people feel for passing pleasures of the senses.
items.core_idea: Love God as fiercely as others love pleasure

items.plain: A little practice of right living and spiritual self-realisation is worth more than tons of empty talk and silly sentiment.
items.core_idea: A little practice outweighs much empty talk

items.plain: Every soul will be perfect in the end; what we are comes from past thoughts and acts, and what we will be from what we do now. Yet we mostly need outside help to awaken the soul's higher powers.
items.core_idea: We shape our destiny, but need outside help

fix.display_text: Every soul is destined to be perfect, and every being, in the end, will attain the state of perfection. Whatever we are now is the result of our acts and thoughts in the past; and whatever we shall be in the future will be the result of what we think and do now. But this, the shaping of our own destinies, does not preclude our receiving help from outside; nay, in the vast majority of cases such help is absolutely necessary. When it comes, the higher powers and possibilities of the soul are quickened, spiritual life is awakened, growth is animated, and man becomes holy and perfect in the end.

items.plain: We can study books our whole lives and become very clever, yet find we have not grown spiritually at all. Great intellect does not always bring equal spiritual growth.
items.core_idea: Intellect does not bring spiritual growth

items.plain: Often when someone we love dies, we feel the world slipping away and resolve to seek something higher and become religious. In a few days the feeling passes, and we are left just where we were.
items.core_idea: Grief's urge toward religion soon fades

items.plain: Truly longing for religion is hard; talks and books do not prove it, only a constant fight with your lower nature until the longing is real. It may take many lifetimes, but whoever perseveres will succeed.
items.core_idea: Real spiritual longing takes endless persistent struggle

items.plain: Ramakrishna told of men in a mango orchard who counted and debated leaves, twigs and branches, while one sensible man simply ate the mangoes. Was he not the wise one?
items.core_idea: Taste the fruit instead of counting leaves

fix.display_text: Bhagavân Ramakrishna used to tell a story of some men who went into a mango orchard and busied themselves in counting the leaves, the twigs, and the branches, examining their colour, comparing their size, and noting down everything most carefully, and then got up a learned discussion on each of these topics, which were undoubtedly highly interesting to them. But one of them, more sensible than the others, did not care for all these things, and instead thereof, began to eat the mango fruit. And was he not wise?

items.plain: Religion, the highest wisdom, cannot be bought or learned from books. Search the Himalayas, the seabed or Tibet and you will not find it until your heart is ready and your teacher has come.
items.core_idea: Wisdom comes when the heart is ready

items.plain: Very few combine wide sympathy with intense love: liberal groups lose their fervour and become social clubs, while narrow sects love their ideal by hating everyone else. If only more people were both intense and broad.
items.core_idea: Few combine intense love with wide sympathy

items.plain: The young plant of spirituality dies if exposed too early to constantly changing ideas. Some, calling it open-mindedness, chase new ideals for the thrill like a craving for drink, and religion becomes a mental drug.
items.core_idea: Chasing endless new ideals kills spiritual growth

items.plain: At first it is very hard to make the mind think of the Lord all the time, but each effort makes the power stronger. As Krishna says in the Gita, it comes through practice and non-attachment.
items.core_idea: Practice makes remembering God easier

items.plain: Anyone can do a good deed on impulse or out of superstition, but the true lover of humanity envies no one. The world's so-called great people grow jealous of one another over a little name, fame or gold.
items.core_idea: True love of humanity is free of jealousy

items.plain: Inner purity alone is better when outward rituals are impractical, but woe to anyone or any nation that forgets the inner essentials and clings to forms. Forms matter only while they express inner life; otherwise destroy them.
items.core_idea: Forms matter only while they express inner life

items.plain: In the West a religious person is pictured gloomy and long-faced, but such people need a doctor; they are not yogis. It is the cheerful mind that perseveres and the strong mind that cuts through a thousand difficulties.
items.core_idea: A cheerful, strong mind perseveres

items.plain: Too much laughter unfits the mind for serious thought and wastes its energy, just as too much gloom does. A strong will yields less to emotion, and spiritual realisation comes only when the mind is steady, peaceful and balanced.
items.core_idea: Realisation needs a steady, balanced mind

items.plain: When the moon shines, the stars fade, and when the sun shines, the moon fades. The renunciation that devotion needs comes not by killing desire but naturally, as weaker lights fade before a growing brighter one.
items.core_idea: Love of God makes lesser desires fade naturally

items.plain: When a ship nears a magnetic rock, its iron bolts are pulled out and its planks float free. In the same way God's grace loosens what binds the soul, and the soul becomes free.
items.core_idea: God's grace loosens what binds the soul

items.plain: The same love, rightly or wrongly directed, makes one person give everything to the poor and another kill and rob. Like fire that can cook a meal or burn a child, the difference lies in how it is used.
items.core_idea: Love's direction makes it good or harmful

items.plain: Step back from the world's petty selfish attachments and watch life as a witness and a student. Inside the current you feel the friction, falls and fights; standing outside it, you see God showing Himself as Love through countless channels.
items.core_idea: As a witness, see God as Love everywhere

items.plain: The Lord is a great magnet and we are iron filings, always drawn toward Him. All our struggle in life, even when people do not know it, is meant to bring us to Him and make us one with Him.
items.core_idea: All life's struggle draws us toward God

items.plain: Pain at lacking money and joy at a handful of coins are feelings aimed wrongly. Pain at not yet reaching God leads to salvation, and joy should serve the highest ideal; the same goes for every feeling.
items.core_idea: Turn every feeling toward the highest ideal

fix.display_text: We find that pleasures and pains are very common and oft-recurring feelings in our lives. When a man feels pain because he has not wealth or some such worldly thing, he is giving a wrong direction to the feeling. Still pain has its uses. Let a man feel pain that he has not reached the Highest, that he has not reached God, and that pain will be to his salvation. When you become glad that you have a handful of coins, it is a wrong direction given to the faculty of joy; it should be given a higher direction, it must be made to serve the Highest Ideal. Pleasure in that kind of ideal must surely be our highest joy. This same thing is true of all our other feelings.

items.plain: Love of God surely brings love of everyone in the universe. The closer we come to God, the more we see all things in Him, and the heart becomes an endless fountain of love.
items.core_idea: Loving God brings love for everyone

items.plain: Intense love for God brings total surrender, the sense that nothing that happens is against us, so the devotee welcomes pain, misery, even death as from the Beloved. Such uncomplaining acceptance is worth more than heroic deeds.
items.core_idea: Loving surrender welcomes even pain as God's gift

items.plain: We can care for our bodies for a while, but they must go. Since death is the one certainty, blessed are those whose bodies are spent serving others; better to die in a good cause than a bad one.
items.core_idea: Spend your body in service of others

items.plain: The delusion that we are only our body, and must protect and please it at all costs, breeds all the world's selfishness. Once you know you are other than your body, there is nothing to fight for and selfishness dies.
items.core_idea: Believing we are the body breeds selfishness

items.plain: Let things come as they will; that is what Thy will be done means, not struggling while assuming God wants our weaknesses and ambitions. If good comes even from our selfish efforts, that is God's business.
items.core_idea: Thy will be done means letting things come

items.plain: Human love usually thrives only when returned, but rarely it goes on without return, like the moth that loves the flame and dies in it. Loving simply because love's nature is to love is the highest, most unselfish love.
items.core_idea: The highest love asks nothing in return

fix.display_text: Ordinarily human love is seen to flourish only in places where it is returned; where love is not returned for love, cold indifference is the natural result. There are, however, rare instances in which we may notice love exhibiting itself even where there is no return of love. We may compare this kind of love, for purposes of illustration, to the love of the moth for the fire; the insect loves the fire, falls into it, and dies. It is indeed in the nature of this insect to love so. To love because it is the nature of love to love is undeniably the highest and the most unselfish manifestation of love that may be seen in the world.

items.plain: Where something is wanted in return, there is no real love, only shopkeeping. While we expect favours from God for our worship, true love cannot grow; those who worship for favours will stop when the favours do not come.
items.core_idea: Love that seeks a reward is shopkeeping

fix.display_text: Wherever there is any seeking for something in return, there can be no real love; it becomes a mere matter of shop-keeping. As long as there is in us any idea of deriving this or that favour from God in return for our respect and allegiance to Him, so long there can be no true love growing in our hearts. Those who worship God because they wish Him to bestow favours on them are sure not to worship Him if those favours are not forthcoming.

items.plain: Begging is not love's language, and worshipping God even for salvation is just as low; love is for love's sake. As a beautiful landscape asks nothing yet fills you with calm and bliss, the devotee simply loves.
items.core_idea: Love is for love's sake, seeking no reward

items.plain: Love conquers fear: a mother who flees a barking dog will leap into a lion's mouth to save her child. Fear comes from making ourselves small and separate; the less we think ourselves insignificant, the less we fear.
items.core_idea: Love conquers fear

items.plain: Some say selfishness drives all human action, but selfishness is just love narrowed. When I see myself as including the whole universe, there is no selfishness; when I mistake myself for something small, my love shrinks.
items.core_idea: Selfishness is love made narrow

items.plain: As you open your heart to a friend who never scolds but always helps, equal love can flow between you and a friendly God. Then God is a near friend to whom you can safely tell your deepest secrets.
items.core_idea: God can be a close, trusted friend

items.plain: The world is a playground and God is our eternal playmate. Misery comes only when we forget it is play and take life's passing events too seriously; see it as a stage where we help Him play, and misery ends.
items.core_idea: See life as God's play and misery ends

fix.display_text: The world is just a playground, and we are here having good fun, having a game; and God is with us playing all the while, and we are with Him playing. God is our eternal playmate. How beautifully He is playing! The play is finished when the cycle comes to an end. There is rest for a shorter or longer time; again all come out and play. It is only when you forget that it is all play and that you are also helping in the play, it is only then that misery and sorrows come. Then the heart becomes heavy, then the world weighs upon you with tremendous power. But as soon as you give up the serious idea of reality as the characteristic of the changing incidents of the three minutes of life and know it to be but a stage on which we are playing, helping Him to play, at once misery ceases for you.

items.plain: The great love we feel for a child, given blindly to any human being, sooner or later brings pain. That pain wakes us up to give our love to the Highest One, who never dies or changes.
items.core_idea: Give your love to the unchanging God

items.plain: God is the goal of all our feelings, so if you must be angry, be angry with Him, your Beloved and Friend. People will react to your anger, but you can safely ask Him why He leaves you alone.
items.core_idea: Bring even your anger to God

items.plain: A man the world called mad answered that the world is a madhouse: some are mad for love, fame, money or heaven, and he is mad for God. Everyone is mad, he said, but his madness is the best.
items.core_idea: Everyone is mad for something; choose God

items.plain: We all start by loving ourselves, and the little self makes love selfish. But at last a blaze of light shows the little self joined with the Infinite, and we realise that Love, the Lover and the Beloved are One.
items.core_idea: Love, Lover and Beloved are One

items.plain: Doing nothing cannot be the goal, or walls and tree stumps would be the wisest of all, and passion is not true activity either. Real activity, as Vedanta sees it, goes with unshakeable calm, the best state for work.
items.core_idea: True action is combined with unshakeable calm

items.plain: He once thought, as many ask, that work needs passion, but experience shows the less passion and the more calm, the better and more we work. Letting feelings loose wastes energy, frays the nerves and achieves little.
items.core_idea: The calmer we are, the better we work

items.plain: The world's great workers were remarkably calm; nothing threw them off balance. Someone who gives way to anger or hatred breaks himself apart and achieves nothing; the calm, forgiving, balanced mind does the most work.
items.core_idea: A calm, forgiving mind does the most work

items.plain: The soul was never born and will never die; fear of death and beliefs about what we cannot do are superstitions, for we can do everything. Vedanta says whoever does not believe in himself is the real atheist.
items.core_idea: Not believing in yourself is the real atheism

items.plain: All the powers of the universe are already ours; we cover our eyes and cry that it is dark, but remove the hands and the light is there. Darkness and weakness never existed; only fools call themselves weak and impure.
items.core_idea: All power is already ours; darkness never existed

items.plain: Vedanta knows no sin, only error, and the worst error is calling yourself weak, sinful or powerless. Each such thought adds a link to your chain and sends a bad thought into the world.
items.core_idea: Calling yourself weak or sinful is the greatest error

items.plain: Human nature resists moving even one step forward. We are like people freezing in snow who beg to keep sleeping because it feels pleasant, and die there; all our lives we freeze from the feet up and still want sleep.
items.core_idea: We resist growth like the freezing who want sleep

items.plain: Condemn no one: help if you can, and if not, bless others and let them go their way. Criticism wastes energy, because in the end we see everyone is nearing the same ideal and our differences are mostly of expression.
items.core_idea: Help or bless others, but never condemn

items.plain: We all know our weaknesses, and dwelling on a disease does not cure it; medicine does. The cure for weakness is not brooding over it but thinking of strength, so teach people the strength already in them.
items.core_idea: Cure weakness by thinking of strength

items.plain: The strongest force in the lives of great people has been faith in themselves, and even someone who sinks very low will one day learn it. Why wait for bitter experience, when faith in ourselves will do everything?
items.core_idea: Faith in yourself will do everything

items.plain: No one knows how much power lies hidden in you; humanity has shown only a tiny part of it in millions of years. So do not call yourself weak, for behind you lies an ocean of infinite power and blessedness.
items.core_idea: Infinite power lies hidden within you

items.plain: You are the Pure One: wake up and rise, mighty one, for this sleep does not suit you. Do not think yourself weak, miserable or a sinner, but show your true, almighty nature.
items.core_idea: Wake up to your pure, mighty nature

items.plain: Whatever leads to oneness is truth. Love is true and hatred false, because hatred divides people and destroys, while love binds and unites.
items.core_idea: Love unites and is true; hatred divides

items.plain: If you feel for others, you are growing toward oneness; without that feeling, even the greatest intellect is dry and worth nothing. If you feel, even unable to read, you are on the right path and the Lord is yours.
items.core_idea: Feeling for others matters more than intellect

items.plain: Vedanta's theme is to see the Lord in everything, and to see things as they really are, not as they seem.
items.core_idea: See the Lord in everything

items.plain: You can make an image to worship God, but a better one already exists: the living person. You can build a temple, but a far higher one already exists: the human body.
items.core_idea: The living person is God's best temple

items.plain: Some truths are uncomfortable until we follow them all the way. Human nature is conservative: once we do something, we find it hard to stop, and the mind resists new ideas because they bring discomfort.
items.core_idea: The mind resists new truths because they discomfort

fix.display_text: There are cases where truth is not comfortable until we reach its climax. Human nature is very conservative. It does something, and having once done that, finds it hard to get out of it. The mind will not receive new thoughts, because they bring discomfort.

items.plain: Religion is always a practical science; there never was and never will be a purely theological religion. Practice comes first, knowledge after.
items.core_idea: In religion, practice comes before knowledge

items.plain: The moment I see God living in every human body and stand in reverence before every person, seeing God in them, everything that binds me falls away and I am free.
items.core_idea: Seeing God in everyone sets you free

items.plain: Vedanta does say each person must have their own path, but the path is not the goal.
items.core_idea: The path is not the goal

items.plain: Love cannot grow out of fear; it rests on freedom. Only when we truly begin to love the world do we understand what the brotherhood of humanity means.
items.core_idea: Love rests on freedom, not fear

fix.display_text: Love cannot come through fear, its basis is freedom. When we really begin to love the world, then we understand what is meant by brotherhood of mankind, and not before.

items.plain: Come out of narrow ruts into the open light, for an infinite soul cannot be content in small grooves. Everything is yours, so embrace it with love; if you have ever wanted to, you have felt God.
items.core_idea: Embracing the universe with love is feeling God

items.plain: Until we know our real nature, we are beggars pushed around and enslaved by every force in nature. We cry for help, even to imaginary beings, and it never comes, yet we keep hoping while a whole life passes.
items.core_idea: Not knowing our nature, we beg for help in vain

items.plain: Be free and expect nothing from anyone; looking back, you will see that the help you hoped for from others never came. All real help came from within, from what you yourself worked for.
items.core_idea: All real help comes from within

items.plain: As the Bible says, if you cannot love the brother you see, how can you love the God you do not? If you cannot see God in a human face, you cannot see Him in clouds or idols.
items.core_idea: Religion begins when you see God in people

items.plain: Always look at others with love and sympathy, knowing they are walking the same path we have already walked.
items.core_idea: See others with love; they walk our path

items.plain: If you are truly pure, how can you see impurity? What is inside shows outside, so we see impurity only when it is in us.
items.core_idea: We see impurity only if it is within us

items.plain: As individuals we seem separate, but in reality we are one. The less we think of ourselves as separate from that One, the better; the more separate we feel from the Whole, the more miserable we become.
items.core_idea: Feeling separate from the Whole brings misery

items.plain: What we need is growth and realisation; no theory ever raised anyone higher and no books can make us purer. The only power is realisation, which lies within us and comes from thinking, so let people think.
items.core_idea: Realisation comes from within, through thinking

items.plain: Infinite power, existence and bliss are already ours. We do not need to gain them; we only need to bring them out.
items.core_idea: Infinite power is already ours to bring out

items.plain: Since childhood everyone around him taught weakness and told him he was weak. It is hard now to realise his own strength, but through analysis and reasoning he comes to know it and realise it.
items.core_idea: Reason can undo a lifetime of being taught weakness

items.plain: When someone gains a better idea, he calls his old ideas harmful and useless, forgetting they were needed to bring him where he is. We all grow by living on crude ideas first and then rising higher.
items.core_idea: Old ideas were steps to where we are

items.plain: We are bound only by laws we make ourselves: our thoughts, words and deeds are the threads of the net we throw around ourselves. Once we set a force in motion, we must take its full consequences.
items.core_idea: Our own deeds weave the net that binds us

items.plain: If you dare to declare that you are free, you are free this moment. If you say you are bound, bound you will stay.
items.core_idea: Declare yourself free and you are free

items.plain: You may dread losing a hundred pounds, while others would not blink at losing everything they own; such people have existed and still do. Why judge them by your own standard?
items.core_idea: Do not judge others by your own limits

items.plain: History shows that those who never thought of their own little selves did the most good for humanity, and the more people think of themselves, the less they can do for others.
items.core_idea: Self-forgetful people help humanity most

items.plain: The key to all goodness is not I but you; never mind heaven, hell or the soul. The world is full of misery, so go into it as the Buddha did and work to lessen it, or die trying.
items.core_idea: Go out and lessen the world's misery

items.plain: Like silkworms, we spin a cocoon from our own substance and end up trapped inside. But not forever: inside it we will grow spiritually and, like the butterfly, come out free.
items.core_idea: We will emerge free from our self-made cocoon

items.plain: He is glad of his many mistakes, since each made him who he is; that is no reason to err on purpose, but do not mope over them. All will come right, because goodness and purity are our indestructible nature.
items.core_idea: Do not mope over mistakes; your goodness remains

items.plain: We make what we call mistakes, rather than sins, because we are weak, and we are weak because we are ignorant. We cover our own eyes and cry that it is dark; remove the hands and the soul's light shines.
items.core_idea: Mistakes come from weakness, weakness from ignorance

items.plain: Wailing about a room that has been dark for thousands of years will not end the darkness, but striking a match will. Brooding over your wrongs does no good; bring in the light and evil goes at once.
items.core_idea: Bring in light instead of lamenting the dark

items.plain: Someone who wants nothing for himself has nothing to fear. What can frighten him, and what fear can death or evil hold for him?
items.core_idea: Who desires nothing fears nothing

items.plain: However busy we are with work, ambitions and struggles, sometimes a pause comes and the mind wants to know what lies beyond this world. At times it glimpses a realm beyond the senses and begins to strive toward it.
items.core_idea: In quiet pauses the mind seeks the beyond

items.plain: Why should everyone think as we do? A rational person should be glad they do not, for he wants to live among thinking people, not in a land like a grave; difference is the first sign of thought.
items.core_idea: Difference is the first sign of thought

items.plain: People never move from error to truth, only from lesser truth to higher truth. What you knew as a child was not foolish; what you know now is that knowledge plus something more.
items.core_idea: We grow from lesser truth to higher truth

items.plain: Photos of the sun taken at each stage of a journey toward it all differ yet show one sun. So each of us sees truth from a standpoint shaped by birth, education and surroundings, yet all share one universal truth.
items.core_idea: We all see one truth from different standpoints

items.plain: Spiritual ideas satisfy only when they come in your own way and speak your soul's language. When someone gives truth in my language, I understand it at once and keep it forever.
items.core_idea: Truth must speak your own soul's language

items.plain: When we start out in life we believe our fate will be extraordinary, and nothing can shake that belief. When we grow old, we think differently.
items.core_idea: Youth expects greatness; age thinks differently

items.plain: Money may come and go and troubles pile up, but if you keep your ideal whole, nothing can kill you, even at a hundred. Once that ideal and mission are lost, all the world's wealth and power cannot save you.
items.core_idea: Keep your ideal alive and nothing can kill you

items.plain: An ideal comes to mind that may only be a dream and may never come true. But sometimes it is better to dream great truths than to die on bad, hard facts, so let us dream.
items.core_idea: Better to dream great truths than die on facts

items.plain: He believes in acceptance, not tolerance, since to tolerate is to think others wrong and merely allow them to live. Is it not blasphemy to think we are allowing others to live?
items.core_idea: Acceptance, not mere tolerance

items.plain: We stand in the present yet open ourselves to the endless future. We take in all of the past, enjoy the light of today, and open every window of the heart to whatever is to come.
items.core_idea: Embrace past, present and future with an open heart

items.plain: Fanaticism is one of the most dangerous diseases. It stirs up all the wickedness in human nature: anger rises, nerves tighten, and people become like tigers.
items.core_idea: Fanaticism turns people into tigers

items.plain: Winter thunderclouds roar without rain, while monsoon clouds silently flood the world; so those who truly feel the brotherhood of humanity show it in their lives, not in talk or little sects. We need more work, less talk.
items.core_idea: Real love shows in deeds, not talk

items.plain: Our faces all differ, yet we are all human. He cannot grasp this shared humanity with the senses, but if he is sure of anything, it is that it is there, common to us all.
items.core_idea: A shared humanity lies beneath all our differences

items.plain: We should not wish everyone thought alike, or there would be nothing to think and we would stare at each other like museum mummies. Our differences are the very soul of progress and of all thought.
items.core_idea: Differences are the soul of progress

items.plain: People fetch water from a lake in cups, jars and buckets, and the water takes each vessel's shape, yet it is all water. Our minds are such vessels: God fills each and appears in its shape, yet He is One.
items.core_idea: God is one, though each mind shapes Him

items.plain: Do not tear anything down; build, and help if you can, or else fold your hands and stand by. If you cannot help, at least do no harm, and never speak against anyone's sincere beliefs.
items.core_idea: Build and help, or at least do no harm
